news.full_article_text: COP17: Global progress on biodiversity targets to be assessed ahead of COP31 COP17 in Armenia’s Yerevan comes at a critical halfway point where countries stand against their commitments Ahead of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Turkey’s Antalya next month, negotiators are gathering in Armenia’s Yerevan for the UN Convention on Biological Diversity’s COP17 from October 19 to 30. Countries will take stock of their collective progress in implementing the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), a landmark agreement adopted in 2022 to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030, at COP17 for the first time. Nearly 200 countries agreed to the framework with 23 targets for 2030, including protecting at least 30% of the world’s land, inland waters and seas, restoring 30% of degraded ecosystems and mobilising at least $200 billion a year for biodiversity from all sources. They pledged $30 billion annually in international public finance, and shifting at least $500 billion a year in subsidies that harm nature. The framework called for biodiversity to be integrated into decision-making and for the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources to be shared more equitably. COP17 comes at a critical halfway point. Where countries stand against their commitments, where implementation is falling short, and what needs to change in the four years remaining until 2030 will be reviewed at COP17. The review will be based primarily on national reports, biodiversity strategies and other evidence submitted by countries. Early assessments have not been particularly reassuring. The UN’s first global assessment of progress, released just ahead of the Yerevan meeting, found that nearly 90% of countries have established national biodiversity targets but fewer than half of the targets assessed are on track. The report has called for faster implementation and greater ambition. The economic and human consequences are equally significant. The decline of ecosystems is often linked to food insecurity, water stress, extreme heat and wildfires, while degradation of forests and other ecosystems can alter rainfall patterns. What will countries be looking at COP17? One of the biggest areas of focus will be whether governments can translate the 2030 targets into actual action. The global review is expected to identify implementation gaps and provide the basis for decisions on how countries can get back on track. Finance will be another major issue. Countries have committed to mobilising $200 billion annually for biodiversity, including $30 billion in international public finance. They have pledged to shift $500 billion in subsidies that are harmful to nature. COP17 will have to consider not just how much money is spent on biodiversity, but whether governments are continuing to finance activities that undermine it. The Cali Fund, established at COP16 in Colombia to share benefits from the commercial use of digital sequence information on genetic resources, will also be on the agenda. Another issue will be the role and rights of indigenous Peoples and local communities, whose knowledge and stewardship are central to biodiversity conservation. Aimee Roberson, executive director at Indigenous-led nonprofit organisation Cultural Survival, said Indigenous Peoples’ ability to protect ecosystems is closely tied to their rights over their territories and their ability to maintain their traditional ways of life. “The cosmovisions, lifeways, and cultures of Indigenous Peoples emerge from our relationships to Mother Earth and include a deep sense of responsibility to care for the ecosystems we all depend on. However, our ability to steward ecosystems and biodiversity depends on maintaining our ancestral and self-determined lifeways, ceremonies, and economies, and relies on uninterrupted access to our lands, waters, and territories. Clearly, upholding the rights of Indigenous Peoples to self-determination and governance of our territories is critical to a future of mutual flourishing for the diversity of life on Mother Earth,” she said. Why does this matter for COP31? The timing is significant. COP17 ends on October 30. Days later, COP31 will begin in Antalya on November 9. Climate change and biodiversity loss are closely connected. Experts say forests, wetlands, mangroves, oceans and other ecosystems protect against climate impacts. Climate change is accelerating biodiversity loss, meaning action on climate without consideration of nature can undermine climate goals. The UNFCCC’s COP31 agenda reflects this overlap, with one of its six global climate action axes specifically focused on “Stewarding Forests, Oceans, and Biodiversity”. Brian O’Donnell, director of Campaign for Nature, said the first global review shows that the world is not on track to meet the biodiversity targets agreed in Montreal. “In light of these findings, COP17 must serve as a turning point. First and foremost, we encourage parties to focus on ensuring delivery of the centrepiece of the global biodiversity agreement -- the target to protect and conserve at least 30% of the planet’s land and ocean by 2030 (30x30),” said O’Donnell. He added that, with renewed leadership and commitment, delivering 30x30 is viable, and achieving it will not only address the leading driver of biodiversity loss, but will advance other priorities related to sustainable development, food supply, national and global security, climate change, and pandemic prevention. “It is critical that a focus on 30x30 and nature finance at COP17 carries into COP31,” said O’Donnell. He added there has been better synergy between the two COPs since COP26 in Glasgow. “That must continue at COP17 and COP31 with a more concrete focus on how to dramatically increase funding for the protection of nature, both for curbing biodiversity loss and mitigating and adapting to climate change.” For India and other developing countries, both COP17 and COP31 remain crucial for assessing progress and securing climate and biodiversity finance. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jasjeev Gandhiok Jasjeev Gandhiok is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times, where he covers environment, climate change, the clean energy transition and wildlife at the National Bureau. Gandhiok has over a decade of experience in journalism and is based in Delhi. He has reported extensively on Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). This includes the region's air pollution woes, a polluted Yamuna and on urban wildlife still thriving in the region. He joined HT in October 2021. Prior to that, he had five-year stint at The Times of India in Delhi, where he also covered Delhi, with a focus on environment and wildlife. bullet_points: COP17: Global progress on biodiversity targets to be assessed ahead of COP31
COP17 in Armenia’s Yerevan comes at a critical halfway point where countries stand against their commitments

Ahead of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Turkey’s Antalya next month, negotiators are gathering in Armenia’s Yerevan for the UN Convention on Biological Diversity’s COP17 from October 19 to 30. Countries will take stock of their collective progress in implementing the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), a landmark agreement adopted in 2022 to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030, at COP17 for the first time.

Nearly 200 countries agreed to the framework with 23 targets for 2030, including protecting at least 30% of the world’s land, inland waters and seas, restoring 30% of degraded ecosystems and mobilising at least $200 billion a year for biodiversity from all sources. They pledged $30 billion annually in international public finance, and shifting at least $500 billion a year in subsidies that harm nature.
The framework called for biodiversity to be integrated into decision-making and for the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources to be shared more equitably.

COP17 comes at a critical halfway point. Where countries stand against their commitments, where implementation is falling short, and what needs to change in the four years remaining until 2030 will be reviewed at COP17. The review will be based primarily on national reports, biodiversity strategies and other evidence submitted by countries.

Early assessments have not been particularly reassuring. The UN’s first global assessment of progress, released just ahead of the Yerevan meeting, found that nearly 90% of countries have established national biodiversity targets but fewer than half of the targets assessed are on track. The report has called for faster implementation and greater ambition.

The economic and human consequences are equally significant. The decline of ecosystems is often linked to food insecurity, water stress, extreme heat and wildfires, while degradation of forests and other ecosystems can alter rainfall patterns.

news.full_article_text: New govt will have its own policies: Keralam Assembly Speaker on KIIFB issue Kottayam, Keralam Legislative Assembly Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan on Monday defended the UDF administration's stand on KIIFB, saying that when a new government comes to power, it might have policies different from the previous one. Radhakrishnan was responding to reporters' queries regarding the recommendations by an expert panel to end the role of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board as a separate fund-raising and project-financing body, calling into question the financial model that has underpinned the state's infrastructure spending. "We cannot expect a new government to follow the steps of the previous administration. The new government will have its own policies different from that of the previous one," he said. In its report tabled in the Keralam Assembly on Thursday, the committee, headed by retired IAS officer Sudha Pillai, said KIIFB's original rationale of raising funds without using the state's borrowing space had lost its relevance, as its borrowings are now counted against that space. The same day Chief Minister V D Satheesan said that the panel has flagged serious financial irregularities, violations of rules and huge financial liabilities on the part of KIIFB. Alleging that KIIFB was functioning as a 'separate empire', the CM had said the state government would examine the findings of the expert panel report and decide on further action. He had also alleged that large amounts of KIIFB funds were used in Kannur district for acquiring huge tracts of land at exorbitant rates and most of it was lying unutilised. Leader of Opposition in the state assembly Pinarayi Vijayan had on Sunday hit back at Satheesan and the government asking what was wrong with KIIFB funds being spent in Kannur. "Is Kannur not in Keralam?" he had asked and alleged that the current UDF administration was trying to sabotage the development in the state. news.headline: Chargesheet filed against 7 for mob lynching Manipuri musician in Delhi over noise complaint
news.story_lead: Chargesheet filed against 7 for mob lynching Manipuri musician in Delhi over noise complaint Chongtham Vikram Singh was allegedly beaten to death by a group of men, including a juvenile, on September 6 after he objected to noise outside his house. The Delhi Police on Monday said they have filed a chargesheet in Saket court against seven persons in connection with the alleged mob lynching of 54-year-old Manipuri musician and music teacher Chongtham Vikram Singh in southeast Delhi’s Kilokari village in September, officers said. Singh was allegedly beaten to death by a group of men, including a juvenile, on September 6 after he objected to noise and commotion outside his house.
news.full_article_text: Chargesheet filed against 7 for mob lynching Manipuri musician in Delhi over noise complaint Chongtham Vikram Singh was allegedly beaten to death by a group of men, including a juvenile, on September 6 after he objected to noise outside his house. The Delhi Police on Monday said they have filed a chargesheet in Saket court against seven persons in connection with the alleged mob lynching of 54-year-old Manipuri musician and music teacher Chongtham Vikram Singh in southeast Delhi’s Kilokari village in September, officers said. Singh was allegedly beaten to death by a group of men, including a juvenile, on September 6 after he objected to noise and commotion outside his house. The chargesheet has been filed under sections of criminal conspiracy, murder by a group of five or more people (mob lynching), murder and house-trespass. Police have named 19-year-old Bharat Kumar, 26-year-old Pramod, 22-year-old Ramzan Khan, 21-year-old Deepanshu, 32-year-old Mohan Vishwakarma, 36-year-old Vijay, and 26-year-old Mannu in the chargesheet. A juvenile was also apprehended in the case. The incident According to police, the incident took place when Chongtham Vikram Singh stepped out of his apartment to dispose of waste and saw a group of men making noise at an eatery opposite his house. When he objected, the men allegedly chased him from the ground floor to the third floor of the building and assaulted him in front of his 20-year-old son. A postmortem examination in the case had found that Singh died of haemorrhagic shock caused by blunt-force injuries to his chest and abdomen. He was taken to Holy Family Hospital around 12.25am on the day of the incident in an unconscious and unresponsive state and died at around 6.32am. The report documented multiple abrasions on his head, face, neck, limbs, chest, abdomen and back, fractures of several ribs on both sides, and a laceration of the spleen. It also recorded around two litres of blood and 160 grams of clotted blood in the abdominal cavity. HT had earlier reported that the FIR stated Singh had been threatened by the same group when he previously objected to the noise. During questioning, the accused allegedly told police they wanted to “teach him a lesson” but did not expect the assault to turn fatal. The accused reportedly worked as eatery staff and delivery executives. Police have been examining all aspects of the case, including whether there was a racial angle to the killing. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jignasa Sinha Jignasa Sinha is a Special Correspondent at Hindustan Times in New Delhi. With more than six years of reporting experience, she covers crime and policing in the national capital. Her beats also include Delhi prisons, the Delhi Fire Services and Delhi courts, while she regularly reports on gender, labour and social justice. Over the course of her career, Jignasa has reported on major criminal investigations, international crime syndicates, high-profile cyber fraud cases, law-and-order developments, protests, disasters and public institutions. Her reporting combines breaking news with in-depth, long form, human interest stories that examine the human impact of public policy, policing and the criminal justice system. In addition to reporting for the newspaper, she contributes to the Hindustan Times website and app, and plays an active role in coordinating on-ground coverage of major developments and breaking news across Delhi. Before joining Hindustan Times, Jignasa worked at The Indian Express newspaper in New Delhi, where she spent five years covering crime, Delhi airport, courts and health. bullet_points: Chargesheet filed against 7 for mob lynching Manipuri musician in Delhi over noise complaint
Chongtham Vikram Singh was allegedly beaten to death by a group of men, including a juvenile, on September 6 after he objected to noise outside his house.

The Delhi Police on Monday said they have filed a chargesheet in Saket court against seven persons in connection with the alleged mob lynching of 54-year-old Manipuri musician and music teacher Chongtham Vikram Singh in southeast Delhi’s Kilokari village in September, officers said.

Singh was allegedly beaten to death by a group of men, including a juvenile, on September 6 after he objected to noise and commotion outside his house. The chargesheet has been filed under sections of criminal conspiracy, murder by a group of five or more people (mob lynching), murder and house-trespass.

Police have named 19-year-old Bharat Kumar, 26-year-old Pramod, 22-year-old Ramzan Khan, 21-year-old Deepanshu, 32-year-old Mohan Vishwakarma, 36-year-old Vijay, and 26-year-old Mannu in the chargesheet. A juvenile was also apprehended in the case.
According to police, the incident took place when Chongtham Vikram Singh stepped out of his apartment to dispose of waste and saw a group of men making noise at an eatery opposite his house.
When he objected, the men allegedly chased him from the ground floor to the third floor of the building and assaulted him in front of his 20-year-old son.

A postmortem examination in the case had found that Singh died of haemorrhagic shock caused by blunt-force injuries to his chest and abdomen. He was taken to Holy Family Hospital around 12.25am on the day of the incident in an unconscious and unresponsive state and died at around 6.32am.

news.headline: 2 Indo-Canadians elected as mayors, another re-elected in Canada’s British Columbia
news.story_lead: 2 Indo-Canadians elected as mayors, another re-elected in Canada’s British Columbia Incumbent mayors were defeated as the polls were held for 161 municipalities and 27 regional districts on Saturday An Indo-Canadian was elected mayor of Fernie while another person of Indian origin was re-elected as Williams Lake’s top city official as municipal election results were declared in Canada’s westernmost province of British Columbia. A third Indo-Canadian was elected the Mission city’s youngest mayor without a contest a month earlier. Incumbent mayors were defeated as the elections were held for 161 municipalities and 27 regional districts on Saturday across British Columbia, where South Asians account for 9.6% of the population, according to the 2021 census.
news.full_article_text: 2 Indo-Canadians elected as mayors, another re-elected in Canada’s British Columbia Incumbent mayors were defeated as the polls were held for 161 municipalities and 27 regional districts on Saturday An Indo-Canadian was elected mayor of Fernie while another person of Indian origin was re-elected as Williams Lake’s top city official as municipal election results were declared in Canada’s westernmost province of British Columbia. A third Indo-Canadian was elected the Mission city’s youngest mayor without a contest a month earlier. Incumbent mayors were defeated as the elections were held for 161 municipalities and 27 regional districts on Saturday across British Columbia, where South Asians account for 9.6% of the population, according to the 2021 census. Harshan Ramadass, better known as Harsh, the Fernie mayor-elect, has an undergraduate degree in mechanical engineering from Bangalore University’s Visvesvaraya College of Engineering and an MBA from the University of British Columbia’s Sauder School of Business. He arrived in Fernie in 2011 to work with a resource company, and his daughter was born there. “I am deeply honoured to be your next mayor, and I look forward to working with our new council and the entire community to turn that vision into action,” MyEastKootenayNow quoted Ramadass as saying. Ramadass, who served on the city council for four years before entering the mayoral fray, said that, having grown up with limited means in India, he knows what it means to stretch every dollar and plan for the long term. “That mindset never leaves you — and it’s exactly the discipline I bring to how I think about public money,” Ramadass, who has worked in mining, automotive, and manufacturing sectors in the US, India, and Canada since 2003, said on his campaign website. Surinderpal Rathor, re-elected as the Williams Lake mayor, was first elected to the city council in 1993. He served seven consecutive terms totalling 21 years, before becoming the mayor in 2022. Rathor arrived in Williams Lake in 1974 after immigrating from India at the age of 21. Jag Gill, another Indo-Canadian, became the youngest Mission mayor a month earlier by acclamation and without a contest on September 18. He was first elected to the city council in 2018, the youngest to do so. After two terms on the council, he sought the mayor’s office. Gill did not expect to win the election without a contest. “I wanted an election. I wanted to keep knocking on doors, put my eight-year record and my vision in front of this community, answer the hard questions, and ask people for their vote,” he said in a letter to the community. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Anirudh Bhattacharyya Anirudh Bhattacharya is a Toronto-based commentator on North American issues, and an author. He has also worked as a journalist in New Delhi and New York spanning print, television and digital media. He tweets as @anirudhb. Read More

news.headline: HT Exclusive| Army to get own communications satellite by mid-2028: Top officials
news.story_lead: HT Exclusive| Army to get own communications satellite by mid-2028: Top officials The Army, unlike the Indian Air Force and the Navy, lacks a dedicated communications satellite and currently relies on the IAF’s GSAT-7A for communication. The Indian Army’s first dedicated communications satellite is expected to be launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) around mid-2028, reinforcing the force’s communications backbone and its operational capabilities, top officials aware of the matter said on Monday. The satellite, GSAT-7B, will provide the army with secure, round-the-clock connectivity across remote border areas and challenging terrain, supporting day-to-day military operations and effective battlefield command and control, the officials said.
news.full_article_text: HT Exclusive| Army to get own communications satellite by mid-2028: Top officials The Army, unlike the Indian Air Force and the Navy, lacks a dedicated communications satellite and currently relies on the IAF’s GSAT-7A for communication. The Indian Army’s first dedicated communications satellite is expected to be launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) around mid-2028, reinforcing the force’s communications backbone and its operational capabilities, top officials aware of the matter said on Monday. The satellite, GSAT-7B, will provide the army with secure, round-the-clock connectivity across remote border areas and challenging terrain, supporting day-to-day military operations and effective battlefield command and control, the officials said. The development is significant because the Army, unlike the Indian Air Force and the Navy, lacks a dedicated communications satellite and currently relies on the IAF’s GSAT-7A to meet its communication requirements. In March 2023, the defence ministry signed a ₹ 3,000-crore contract with NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), ISRO’s commercial arm, to develop the advanced communications satellite for the army—a step towards addressing a long-standing requirement. Details The launch, initially scheduled for November 2027, will be delayed by six months due to technical reasons, the officials added, asking not to be named. The five-tonne geostationary satellite, India’s heaviest communications satellite to date, is designed to provide beyond-line-of-sight communications for deployed troops and military formations, as well as weapon systems, airborne platforms, and other mission-critical assets. Space-based communications will be critical during conflict, providing resilient communication links when terrestrial networks are disrupted or damaged by enemy action, the officials said. To be sure, China is rapidly expanding its space capabilities and could potentially disable or knock out satellites. It is known to have the capability to disrupt satellite signals using jammers and other anti-satellite technologies. Another dedicated satellite for IAF Last week, the defence ministry signed a ₹ 2,563-crore contract with NSIL for another dedicated communications satellite, GSAT-7C, for the IAF. The indigenously designed, developed, and manufactured satellite will enhance secure, resilient, and seamless communication capabilities for the IAF's assets, thereby strengthening operational effectiveness, it said. ISRO launched the Navy’s GSAT-7R communications satellite last November, a replacement for the Rukmini satellite. The home-grown satellite enables seamless and secure communications between warships, aircraft, submarines and maritime operations centres. Indian military's space focus The Indian military's focus on space has been steadily growing. It released the Joint Military Space Doctrine last September during the Combined Commanders’ Conference in Kolkata, a significant step towards institutionalising space as a key domain of national security and integrating it into the country’s defence strategy. The country is also formulating a National Military Space Policy to safeguard its space-based assets, strengthen military capabilities and address emerging security challenges in the space domain. The satellite, GSAT-7B, will provide the army with secure, round-the-clock connectivity across remote border areas and challenging terrain, supporting day-to-day military operations and effective battlefield command and control, the officials said.

In March 2023, the defence ministry signed a ₹ 3,000-crore contract with NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), ISRO’s commercial arm, to develop the advanced communications satellite for the army—a step towards addressing a long-standing requirement.
The launch, initially scheduled for November 2027, will be delayed by six months due to technical reasons, the officials added, asking not to be named.

Space-based communications will be critical during conflict, providing resilient communication links when terrestrial networks are disrupted or damaged by enemy action, the officials said.

static_gk: Reserve Bank of India (RBI): Established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Repo Rate: The rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends money to commercial banks to meet short-term funding requirements.
news.headline: RBI Repo Rate Hike: Evaluating Loan EMI Increase Versus Tenure Extension
news.story_lead: With monetary policy tightening leading to increases in the Reserve Bank of India's repo rate, home loan borrowers with floating interest rates face higher borrowing costs. Debtors must choose between increasing their Equated Monthly Instalment (EMI) or extending their loan tenure to manage the repayment burden.
news.full_article_text:
### Impact of Repo Rate Hikes on Retail Loans

When the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) increases the repo rate, commercial banks and financial institutions adjust their marginal cost of funds-based lending rates (MCLR) or external benchmark-linked lending rates (EBLR). Consequently, existing and new borrowers holding floating-rate home loans face elevated interest charges.

### Strategic Choices for Borrowers

Borrowers faced with an upward interest rate adjustment generally have two primary financial paths to restructure their loans:

* **Increasing the Monthly EMI:** By opting to raise the monthly payment amount, borrowers maintain their original loan tenure. This option increases immediate monthly cash outflows but prevents an expansion of the total interest burden over the lifespan of the debt.
* **Extending the Loan Tenure:** By opting to keep the monthly payment amount unchanged, the financial institution extends the overall repayment period. While this preserves immediate monthly liquidity, it significantly increases the overall cumulative interest payable.

### Prepayment and Risk Mitigation Strategies

Financial experts emphasize that extending loan tenures—especially during the early stages of a loan—can drastically increase the total repayment burden. Making partial prepayments or choosing a hybrid approach combining a moderate EMI increase with a minimal tenure adjustment helps borrowers mitigate long-term interest inflation.
bullet_points: A repo rate increase by the RBI leads to higher floating-rate home loan interest rates across commercial banks.
Borrowers face a choice between increasing monthly EMI payouts or extending loan tenure.
Opting for a higher EMI keeps the original repayment timeline intact and minimizes total cumulative interest.
Extending tenure protects short-term monthly cash flow but substantially increases total interest costs over time.
The impact of tenure extension is most severe during the initial years of a home loan when interest forms a larger portion of the EMI.
Partial prepayments serve as an effective mechanism to counter interest rate hikes.
key_facts: Repo rate hikes lead directly to higher floating interest rates on home loans.
Extending repayment tenure keeps the current EMI constant but raises total interest costs.
Increasing the EMI amount keeps loan duration constant and limits cumulative interest expenses.

While repo rate hikes are intended to curb inflation by reducing liquidity, they increase household debt service obligations. Managing retail credit strategy requires balancing immediate cash liquidity against total interest accumulation over long loan tenures.

Higher monthly EMI obligations or longer debt service periods for households.
way_forward: Borrowers should evaluate personal cash flow before deciding between an EMI increase or tenure extension.
Regular partial prepayments should be considered to reduce overall loan interest liabilities during high-rate regimes.

hindi_translation.story_lead: भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा रेपो दर में वृद्धि के बाद, फ्लोटिंग ब्याज दर वाले होम लोन ग्राहकों के लिए कर्ज की लागत बढ़ गई है। ग्राहकों को अपनी मासिक किस्त (ईएमआई) बढ़ाने या पुनर्भुगतान की अवधि बढ़ाने में से किसी एक विकल्प का चयन करना होगा।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### होम लोन पर रेपो रेट में बढ़ोतरी का प्रभाव

जब भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक (आरबीआई) रेपो रेट में वृद्धि करता है, तो वाणिज्यिक बैंक अपने कर्ज देने की दरों को बढ़ा देते हैं। इसके फलस्वरूप, फ्लोटिंग-रेट होम लोन वाले ग्राहकों पर ब्याज का भार बढ़ जाता है।

### उधारकर्ताओं के लिए रणनीतिक विकल्प

ब्याज दरों में वृद्धि के बाद ग्राहकों के पास दो मुख्य विकल्प उपलब्ध होते हैं:

* **मासिक ईएमआई बढ़ाना:** मासिक भुगतान राशि बढ़ाने से लोन की मूल अवधि नहीं बदलती। यह विकल्प तत्काल मासिक खर्च को तो बढ़ाता है, लेकिन कुल ब्याज के बोझ को नियंत्रित रखता है।
* **ऋण अवधि बढ़ाना:** मासिक ईएमआई समान रखने पर बैंक लोन की कुल अवधि बढ़ा देते हैं। इससे मासिक बजट तो स्थिर रहता है, लेकिन कुल ब्याज भुगतान बहुत अधिक बढ़ जाता है।

### अंतर-संसदीय जुड़ाव

वियतनाम और स्विट्जरलैंड ने अपने द्विपक्षीय संबंधों को और मजबूत करने के लिए संसदीय सहयोग बढ़ाने की घोषणा की है। यह प्रयास दोनों देशों की विधानसभाओं के बीच संवाद बढ़ाने और शासन व नीतिगत मामलों पर विचारों के आदान-प्रदान को बढ़ावा देने पर केंद्रित है।

अंतर-संसदीय आदान-प्रदान के माध्यम से दोनों देश मजबूत संस्थागत संबंध बनाने और व्यापक राजनीतिक, आर्थिक तथा राजनयिक सहयोग को बढ़ावा देने का लक्ष्य रखते हैं।

news.headline: India Joins 24 Nations in Global Initiative on 6G Technology
news.story_lead: India has partnered with 24 countries in a global initiative focused on the development and deployment of 6G technology. The initiative aims to foster international cooperation, establish global standards, and enhance security in next-generation telecommunications.
news.full_article_text:
### Global 6G Technology Initiative

India has officially partnered with 24 other nations in a major global initiative aimed at advancing sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication technology. The collaborative effort seeks to build a secure, open, and interoperable telecom ecosystem worldwide.

- **International Alliance:** India joins a group of 24 countries to collaborate on joint research, development, and standardisation of 6G networks.
- **Key Objectives:** The initiative focuses on establishing common global benchmarks, strengthening supply chain security, and ensuring technology interoperability across borders.
- **Strategic Value:** By joining this multilateral partnership, India aims to play a central role in shaping international rules and technical standards for emerging technologies rather than adopting them post-development.
bullet_points: India has partnered with 24 countries in a joint global initiative on 6G technology.
The coalition aims to foster international collaboration in 6G research and standardisation.
Key focus areas include network security, open architectures, and global interoperability.
The initiative positions member nations to jointly shape global telecom policies and technical benchmarks.
key_facts: India joined 24 other nations in a global initiative on 6G technology.
Announcement date: October 19, 2026.
important_dates: 2026-10-19: India reported joining the 24-nation 6G technology initiative.
exam_relevance: Prelims: International groupings and technology initiatives related to 6G.
Mains (GS Paper 3): Science and Technology - developments and their applications; Indigenisation of technology and critical communications infrastructure.
news.upsc_analysis: India's participation in the 24-nation 6G coalition demonstrates its commitment to being a active contributor to next-generation telecommunications standards. Early engagement in global tech alliances ensures India's security needs, industrial capacity, and technological standards are aligned with global benchmarks.
causes: The need for unified global standards, robust cybersecurity measures, and joint research in emerging 6G technologies.
impacts: Enhances India's standing in global technology governance.
Facilitates collaborative research and interoperability for next-generation telecommunications networks.
government_steps: Partnered with 24 nations in a global initiative on 6G technology development and standardisation.
way_forward: Strengthen domestic R&D capabilities and foster industry-academia collaboration to contribute effectively to global 6G standardisation.
news.mains_notes: India's inclusion in a 25-nation 6G alliance highlights the growing importance of tech diplomacy. Participating in standard-setting initiatives allows India to protect national security interests, foster indigenous innovation, and build resilient supply chains in critical communication infrastructure.
mains_questions: Examine the strategic importance of international technological partnerships in shaping global 6G standards.
How can India leverage global technology coalitions to strengthen its domestic telecom manufacturing and R&D ecosystem?

prelims_facts: India is part of a 25-nation collaborative initiative focused on 6G wireless technology standards.

hindi_translation.headline: भारत 6G प्रौद्योगिकी पर वैश्विक पहल में 24 देशों के साथ शामिल हुआ
hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत ने 6G तकनीक के विकास और तैनाती पर ध्यान केंद्रित करने वाली एक वैश्विक पहल में 24 अन्य देशों के साथ भागीदारी की है। इस पहल का उद्देश्य अंतरराष्ट्रीय सहयोग को बढ़ावा देना, वैश्विक मानक स्थापित करना और अगली पीढ़ी के दूरसंचार में सुरक्षा बढ़ाना है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### 6G प्रौद्योगिकी पर वैश्विक पहल

भारत आधिकारिक तौर पर छठी पीढ़ी (6G) की वायरलेस संचार तकनीक को आगे बढ़ाने के उद्देश्य से एक प्रमुख वैश्विक पहल में 24 अन्य देशों के साथ शामिल हो गया है। इस सहयोगात्मक प्रयास का उद्देश्य दुनिया भर में एक सुरक्षित, खुला और अंतर-संचालनीय दूरसंचार पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र का निर्माण करना है।

- **अंतर्राष्ट्रीय गठबंधन:** भारत 6G नेटवर्क के संयुक्त अनुसंधान, विकास और मानकीकरण पर सहयोग करने के लिए 24 भागीदार देशों के समूह में शामिल हुआ है।
- **प्रमुख उद्देश्य:** यह पहल सामान्य वैश्विक मानदंड स्थापित करने, आपूर्ति श्रृंखला सुरक्षा को मजबूत करने और सीमाओं के पार प्रौद्योगिकी की अंतर-संचालनीयता सुनिश्चित करने पर केंद्रित है।
- **रणनीतिक महत्व:** इस बहुपक्षीय साझेदारी में शामिल होकर, भारत का लक्ष्य केवल बाहरी मानदंडों को अपनाने के बजाय उभरती प्रौद्योगिकियों के लिए अंतर्राष्ट्रीय नियमों और तकनीकी मानकों को आकार देने में केंद्रीय भूमिका निभाना है।

news.headline: Reserve Bank of India Increases Repo Rate to 5.50% to Manage Inflation Dynamics
news.story_lead: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has adjusted its key monetary policy instrument, raising the repo rate to 5.50 percent. The move is designed to anchor inflationary pressures while maintaining macroeconomic stability and sustainable economic expansion.
news.full_article_text:
Monetary Policy Revision

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has updated its policy rates, increasing the benchmark repo rate to 5.50 percent. The repo rate is the interest rate at which the central bank provides liquidity and short-term loans to commercial banks across the country against eligible securities.

Impact on Borrowing and Inflation

This monetary tightening measures directly influence borrowing costs across commercial banks, affecting loan interest rates for consumer finance, housing, and corporate credit. By raising the policy rate, the central bank aims to control money supply growth and mitigate future inflationary risks while preserving economic stability.
bullet_points: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has increased the benchmark repo rate to 5.50%.
Repo rate is the rate at which commercial banks borrow short-term capital from the central bank.
The policy action aims to manage market liquidity and curb inflationary risks.
A higher repo rate increases borrowing costs for commercial banks, which translates to higher lending rates for consumers.
The rate revision impacts retail loans, corporate credit, and overall demand in the economy.
This move reflects the central bank's priority on price stability and inflation control.
key_facts: Revised Policy Repo Rate: 5.50%
Central Institution: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Primary Objective: Inflation management and economic stability
important_dates: 2026-10-19: Date of report on RBI repo rate revision
exam_relevance: Prelims: Core definitions and concepts of Repo Rate, Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), and monetary policy tools.
Mains: Analysis of monetary policy transmission, central bank instruments, and balancing economic growth with price stability.
news.upsc_analysis: The RBI's decision to increase the repo rate to 5.50% reflects a proactive monetary policy approach focused on anchoring inflation expectations. While rate hikes help check liquidity and curb inflation, they also raise interest rates for businesses and retail borrowers, requiring continuous calibration between price stability and economic growth.
causes: Need to mitigate future inflationary pressures in the economy.
Management of liquidity conditions within the financial system.
impacts: Increase in lending rates for retail, home, and corporate loans.
Moderation in credit growth and money supply within the economy.
challenges: Ensuring that higher borrowing costs do not negatively impact broader GDP growth.
Managing financial stress in interest-sensitive sectors like real estate and auto.
government_steps: Implementation of policy rate adjustment by the Reserve Bank of India raising the repo rate to 5.50%.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 - provides the legal framework for monetary policy formulation and implementation in India.
way_forward: Close monitoring of consumer price index inflation and economic growth indicators to calibrate future policy rate decisions.
news.mains_notes: The RBI repo rate adjustment to 5.50% highlights monetary policy transmission mechanisms. Fluctuations in policy rates regulate liquidity, commercial bank interest rates, and overall demand, playing a key role in managing economic cycles.
mains_questions: Explain the concept of Repo Rate and analyze how monetary policy adjustments by the Reserve Bank of India influence inflation and economic growth.
Discuss the challenges faced by central banks in balancing price stability with economic growth in developing economies like India.
news.takeaway: The Reserve Bank of India has raised its key repo rate to 5.50% to control inflation and maintain economic stability.
prelims_facts: Repo Rate: The rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities.
Current RBI Repo Rate: Increased to 5.50%.

मौद्रिक नीति में संशोधन

भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) ने अपनी नीतिगत दरों को अपडेट करते हुए बेंचमार्क रेपो दर को बढ़ाकर 5.50 प्रतिशत कर दिया है। रेपो दर वह ब्याज दर है जिस पर केंद्रीय बैंक पात्र प्रतिभूतियों के बदले देश भर के वाणिज्यिक बैंकों को तरलता और अल्पकालिक ऋण प्रदान करता है।

ऋण और मुद्रास्फीति पर प्रभाव

मौद्रिक नीति का यह सख्त कदम वाणिज्यिक बैंकों की उधार लागत को सीधे प्रभावित करता है, जिससे उपभोक्ता ऋण, आवास ऋण और कॉर्पोरेट क्रेडिट के लिए ब्याज दरें प्रभावित होती हैं। नीतिगत दर बढ़ाकर, केंद्रीय बैंक का लक्ष्य धन की आपूर्ति की वृद्धि को नियंत्रित करना और भविष्य के मुद्रास्फीति जोखिमों को कम करना है।

रेपो दर वह दर है जिस पर वाणिज्यिक बैंक केंद्रीय बैंक से अल्पकालिक पूंजी उधार लेते हैं।
इस नीतिगत निर्णय का उद्देश्य बाजार की तरलता को प्रबंधित करना और मुद्रास्फीति के जोखिमों को रोकना है।
उच्च रेपो दर वाणिज्यिक बैंकों की उधार लागत बढ़ाती है, जो उपभोक्ताओं के लिए उच्च ऋण दरों में बदल जाती है।
दर संशोधन का प्रभाव खुदरा ऋण, कॉर्पोरेट क्रेडिट और अर्थव्यवस्था में समग्र मांग पर पड़ता है।

news.headline: Tiger Shroff escapes unhurt after shots fired at actor in Mumbai, Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims attack
news.story_lead: Tiger Shroff escapes unhurt after shots fired at actor in Mumbai, Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims attack Three motorcycle-borne men opened fire on actor Tiger Shroff, leaving two people, including his driver injured, police said. Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after three motorcycle-borne men opened fire at him in Juhu area of Mumbai on Sunday evening. Three people, including his driver and an autorickshaw driver, were injured in the incident, police said.
news.full_article_text: Tiger Shroff escapes unhurt after shots fired at actor in Mumbai, Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims attack Three motorcycle-borne men opened fire on actor Tiger Shroff, leaving two people, including his driver injured, police said. Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after three motorcycle-borne men opened fire at him in Juhu area of Mumbai on Sunday evening. Three people, including his driver and an autorickshaw driver, were injured in the incident, police said. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang has claimed the attack after gangster Anil Pandit said he, along with Harman Sandhu, was behind the attack. However, the Mumbai Police has not confirmed on the Bishnoi gang's alleged involvement in the case. Also read: 'Anyone who works with Salman Khan will be next': After attack on Tiger Shroff, Lawrence Bishnoi gang issues fresh threat Deep Dive “We had called him and tried to explain things to him, but he did not understand. So today, we made sure to explain it to him properly,” the post said in Hindi. Pandit warned that until the actors stop working with Bollywood actor Salman Khan , the attacks will continue. “Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next. Wait and watch.” According to initial information, Shroff was returning after playing football at a club when the three unidentified assailants opened fire near Pushpa Park in Juhu . Three people have reportedly been injured, including Shroff's driver Firdos who suffered injuries on his hand, police said. Upon receiving news of the incident, the Mumbai Police officials and ambulances arrived at the scene. The police have cordoned off the area and fifteen police teams have been dispatched to trace the assailants. Currently, the police are examining footage from CCTV cameras installed in the vicinity. The primary reason behind the shooting and the motive of the attackers remain unclear and the probe underway will ascertain that, officials said. The incident has caused a stir within the film industry and the Juhu locality. On February 1, unidentified bike-borne assailants opened fire outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's Juhu residence shortly after midnight. Multiple rounds were fired at the building, though no one was injured. Around 12:45 a.m., two or more attackers on a motorbike discharged five rounds of gunfire at the first floor of Shetty's nine-story building. One bullet struck the glass of a gym in the building; no injuries were reported.

news.headline: 'Anyone who works with Salman Khan will be next': After attack on Tiger Shroff, Lawrence Bishnoi gang issues fresh threat
news.story_lead: 'Anyone who works with Salman Khan will be next': After attack on Tiger Shroff, Lawrence Bishnoi gang issues fresh threat A social media post linked with Lawrence Bishnoi gang's Anil Pandit said he along with Anil Harman Sandhu was behind the attack. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang, which claimed responsibility for opening fire at actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening, warned that anyone in the Mumbai film industry who refuses to heed its warnings or works with actor Salman Khan would be next. However, Mumbai Police have not confirmed any links between the gang and the attack.
news.full_article_text: 'Anyone who works with Salman Khan will be next': After attack on Tiger Shroff, Lawrence Bishnoi gang issues fresh threat A social media post linked with Lawrence Bishnoi gang's Anil Pandit said he along with Anil Harman Sandhu was behind the attack. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang, which claimed responsibility for opening fire at actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening, warned that anyone in the Mumbai film industry who refuses to heed its warnings or works with actor Salman Khan would be next. However, Mumbai Police have not confirmed any links between the gang and the attack. In a purported social media post, Lawrence Bishnoi gang's Anil Pandit claimed that he and Harman Sandhu were behind the attack. “We, Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, take responsibility for what happened to Tiger Shroff today. We had called him and tried to make him understand, but he did not listen. So today, we made sure to teach him a lesson properly,” the post read. Deep Dive “Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next. Wait and watch.” “Note: Some dogs from other groups who think they can gain fame by using our name will soon be killed and made famous,” it added. When the attack unfold According to preliminary information, Shroff was returning after playing football at a club when the three unidentified assailants opened fire near Pushpa Park in Juhu. Three people have reportedly been injured, including Shroff's driver Firdos who suffered injuries on his hand, police said. Mumbai police personnel and ambulances rushed to the spot after receiving information about the incident. The area has been cordoned off, and a search is underway to trace the attackers. Police are also examining CCTV footage from cameras installed in the surrounding area. Ballistics experts were called in at the place where the firing took place to gather the shell casings. Officials said the motive behind the shooting remains unclear and will be established as the investigation progresses. The incident has caused concern in the film industry and the Juhu locality. An eye witness told the police that Shroff was about to sit in his BMW car when the firing took place. Ballistics experts were called in at the place where the firing took place to gather the shell casings. Previous attacks On February 1, unidentified assailants on a motorcycle opened fire outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty ’s residence in Juhu shortly after midnight. The attackers fired multiple rounds at the nine-storey building, with one bullet hitting the glass of a gym on the first floor. No injuries were reported in the incident, which took place around 12.45 am. On October 12, 2024, veteran politician and Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) leader Baba Siddique , 66, was shot dead outside his son Zeeshan Siddique’s office near the Kherwadi signal junction in Bandra East at around 9.30 pm. news.headline: Kochi Mini Cooper crash: Driver’s mother appeals for privacy, extends condolences to victims’ families
news.story_lead: Kochi Mini Cooper crash: Driver’s mother appeals for privacy, extends condolences to victims’ families Suhail Sajeev’s mother said the investigation into the Mini Cooper crash must proceed in the right direction and that the truth must prevail A week after a 19-year-old rammed a Mini Cooper into a scooter, killing three people near Kochi, his mother appealed to the public to give her family some privacy as they navigate the aftermath of the horrific crash. Nooha Sajeev, who runs apparel stores in Kochi and Alappuzha under the brand ‘Iha Designs’, is the mother of Suhail Sajeev, who was arrested on October 11 in connection with the car accident that claimed three lives. In a video posted on Facebook, Nooha expressed her condolences to the families of the three victims.
news.full_article_text: Kochi Mini Cooper crash: Driver’s mother appeals for privacy, extends condolences to victims’ families Suhail Sajeev’s mother said the investigation into the Mini Cooper crash must proceed in the right direction and that the truth must prevail A week after a 19-year-old rammed a Mini Cooper into a scooter, killing three people near Kochi, his mother appealed to the public to give her family some privacy as they navigate the aftermath of the horrific crash. Nooha Sajeev, who runs apparel stores in Kochi and Alappuzha under the brand ‘Iha Designs’, is the mother of Suhail Sajeev, who was arrested on October 11 in connection with the car accident that claimed three lives. In a video posted on Facebook, Nooha expressed her condolences to the families of the three victims. "We have lost three valuable lives. I convey my condolences to their families. I can understand the pain they must be feeling. We raise our children with a lot of hopes and dreams, and when they suddenly leave us, it is unthinkable. My words can never compensate for their grief," Nooha said in the video. Also Read | Mini Cooper driver who killed 3 in Kochi car crash had 5 times legal blood alcohol limit, say police She said that the investigation must proceed in the right direction and that only truth must prevail. Nooha also requested the public to desist from spreading half-truths and give her family some privacy. "This issue is being discussed a lot on social media. Many people are angry at us. But I want to appeal for privacy for me and my family. There are a lot of half-truths going around. Please understand that I am also a woman and a mother hailing from an ordinary family. I am concerned about my son's future just as I am deeply sad about the three people who lost their lives," she said. The 19-year-old’s mother said she felt utterly “helpless” and had been unable to even sit up over the past few days. "Please remember that I have a family of four. We also have lives to go about," she said. This is the first time Nooha Sajeev has spoken publicly about the fallout of the October 11 car crash that led to her younger son, Suhail, being jailed. Nooha had gifted him the Mini Cooper on his birthday this year and shared the moment on Facebook. She had said then that both her sons were car enthusiasts and that she was “happy” to gift the luxury car to her younger son. Around 1:45 am on October 11, Suhail’s Mini Cooper rammed into the rear of a scooter on the road leading to Cochin International Airport near Nedumbassery. Devika, Gopika and Iyas, all in their early 20s, were riding the scooter at the time. They worked at a crafts retail shop and succumbed to their injuries. Suhail was charged with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, while three of his friends, who were in the car at the time of the accident, were booked for abetment. Police found that Suhail and his friends were heavily intoxicated at the time of the crash. Suhail’s blood alcohol concentration was found to be five times the legal limit for driving in India. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Vishnu Varma Vishnu Varma is Assistant Editor and reports from Kerala for the Hindustan Times. He has 10 years of experience writing for print and digital platforms and has worked at The New York Times, NDTV and The Indian Express in the past. news.headline: CJP alleges Ashutosh, Saurav not being released; Delhi Police file FIR over threats to magistrate
news.story_lead: CJP alleges Ashutosh, Saurav not being released; Delhi Police file FIR over threats to magistrate On October 14, he noted that Ranka and Das, who had previously signed a surety bond on October 11 to keep peace, breached it by entering Jantar Mantar. Almost four days after the Cockroach Janta Party's co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to judicial custody for unfurling the national flag at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, the CJP has accused the Delhi Police of intentionally delaying the release of Ranka and Das for days and not accepting the surety bonds submitted by them. The Delhi Police on Sunday said the SEM hearing the case has received threats and lodged an FIR.
news.full_article_text: CJP alleges Ashutosh, Saurav not being released; Delhi Police file FIR over threats to magistrate On October 14, he noted that Ranka and Das, who had previously signed a surety bond on October 11 to keep peace, breached it by entering Jantar Mantar. Almost four days after the Cockroach Janta Party's co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to judicial custody for unfurling the national flag at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, the CJP has accused the Delhi Police of intentionally delaying the release of Ranka and Das for days and not accepting the surety bonds submitted by them. The Delhi Police on Sunday said the SEM hearing the case has received threats and lodged an FIR. Police denied allegations of delay and said due procedure is being followed. A special executive magistrate at Mandir Marg is yet to give an order to release the duo. Follow live updates on the Delhi protest here . Ranka and Das in judicial custody Deep Dive "Accordingly, it is hereby ordered that notice under Section 130 BNSS be issued to the respondents. Since no sound surety has been produced at this stage, and to maintain public peace and order, the respondents are remanded to Judicial Custody for a period of five days. List the matter on 19.10.26 for further enquiry," reads the order. Ranka and Das, along with a few other CJP members, had jumped gates to enter the de-notified Jantar Mantar protest site to unfurl the national flag on October 13. They were detained at the same time and put under arrest. Also Read | Delhi Police lodge 3 FIRs over CJP's Tiranga march; Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora released ‘Every day is a new struggle’: CJP national secretary The CJP said that since October 15, they have filed multiple surety bonds to get Ranka and Das released from judicial custody, but police are giving new excuses all the time. Aafreen Nawaz, CJP national secretary, told HT, “We have been sitting like watchdogs at the Mandir Marg police station for four days now. We were told that they will be released once we give surety bonds. Since then, we have been submitting it but they are rejecting. Also, we have been given so many excuses.” “At times, the SHO comes in the evening and not in the morning. The IO tells us he's stuck in traffic and arrives in the evening. One day, DCP Sachin Sharma delayed and didn't sign the bond. They then said our fixed deposits are not proper. But they already have bank stamps. They then said the names of the persons mentioned there don't have a Delhi address. They started picking up our volunteers and threatened them,” Nawaz added. "Every day is a new struggle. We have now filed multiple surety bonds. Taken help from top Supreme Court lawyers, but the police are not ready to accept. Today, they told Ratna Singh (CJP legal affairs head) that the SEM is getting threats if he releases the duo, and a new magistrate needs to come. The SEM also told the lawyers that Abhijeet, while leaving Delhi today, said the party needs to strategise. But he didn't mean any planning or protest. They are nitpicking statements from videos, delaying and giving lame excuses. Tomorrow, I'm sure there will be a holiday, and the procedure will get delayed again," the CJP national secretary stated. ‘They keep giving excuses’: Ratna Ratna on X has been sharing about the delay since Friday. On Sunday, she told the media, “The hearing was supposed to happen at 12 noon but was delayed till 5 pm. Today, everything was complete, the verification was done, and all requirements were met.” "Within about five minutes of the proceedings, the SEM told the court that he had received a threatening message and said he would come tomorrow. It was then that they started accusing us of sending the message. How is it related to the case? They keep giving excuses by not verifying sureties, or approving FDs. It was visible how they orchestrated this. We have followed all procedures, but they are not even ready to listen to the case. This is a conspiracy by Delhi Police. They just want to extend custody," Ratna noted. Meanwhile, the Delhi Police has not officially released a statement on the allegations, delay, and release of the duo. Ranka and Das have been lodged in Tihar jail since October 14. Also Read | CJP to 'restrategise after Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka's release': Abhijeet Dipke on anti-CEC stir ‘Faulty surety bonds’: What the police said Senior police officers said no delay was there and an FIR has been lodged on Sunday in New Delhi district for threatening the SEM Mandir Marg. The FIR was filed in SEM's c complaint under sections of criminal intimidation and threat. A senior police officer said, “They have been filing faulty surety bonds, and we can't accept them. We have to follow procedure. On Sunday evening, the SEM informed us he received threatening messages from CJP about the bail. He said he can't do the job under threat and at such risk. We have to delay the hearing. We have filed an FIR and are conducting an enquiry.” - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jignasa Sinha Jignasa Sinha is a Special Correspondent at Hindustan Times in New Delhi. With more than six years of reporting experience, she covers crime and policing in the national capital. Her beats also include Delhi prisons, the Delhi Fire Services and Delhi courts, while she regularly reports on gender, labour and social justice. Over the course of her career, Jignasa has reported on major criminal investigations, international crime syndicates, high-profile cyber fraud cases, law-and-order developments, protests, disasters and public institutions. Her reporting combines breaking news with in-depth, long form, human interest stories that examine the human impact of public policy, policing and the criminal justice system. In addition to reporting for the newspaper, she contributes to the Hindustan Times website and app, and plays an active role in coordinating on-ground coverage of major developments and breaking news across Delhi. Before joining Hindustan Times, Jignasa worked at The Indian Express newspaper in New Delhi, where she spent five years covering crime, Delhi airport, courts and health. She began her journalism career as an intern at an AI magazine in Bengaluru while pursuing her postgraduate diploma in multimedia journalism at the Indian Institute of Journalism and New Media. They then said the names of the persons mentioned there don't have a Delhi address. They started picking up our volunteers and threatened them,” Nawaz added. "Every day is a new struggle. We have now filed multiple surety bonds. Taken help from top Supreme Court lawyers, but the police are not ready to accept. Today, they told Ratna Singh (CJP legal affairs head) that the SEM is getting threats if he releases the duo, and a new magistrate needs to come. The SEM also told the lawyers that Abhijeet, while leaving Delhi today, said the party needs to strategise. But he didn't mean any planning or protest. They are nitpicking statements from videos, delaying and giving lame excuses. Tomorrow, I'm sure there will be a holiday, and the procedure will get delayed again," the CJP national secretary stated. ‘They keep giving excuses’: Ratna Ratna on X has been sharing about the delay since Friday. On Sunday, she told the media, “The hearing was supposed to happen at 12 noon but was delayed till 5 pm. Today, everything was complete, the verification was done, and all requirements were met.” "Within about five minutes of the proceedings, the SEM told the court that he had received a threatening message and said he would come tomorrow. It was then that they started accusing us of sending the message. How is it related to the case? They keep giving excuses by not verifying sureties, or approving FDs. It was visible how they orchestrated this. We have followed all procedures, but they are not even ready to listen to the case. This is a conspiracy by Delhi Police. They just want to extend custody," Ratna noted. Meanwhile, the Delhi Police has not officially released a statement on the allegations, delay, and release of the duo. Ranka and Das have been lodged in Tihar jail since October 14. Also Read | CJP to 'restrategise after Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka's release': Abhijeet Dipke on anti-CEC stir ‘Faulty surety bonds’: What the police said Senior police officers said no delay was there and an FIR has been lodged on Sunday in New Delhi district for threatening the SEM Mandir Marg. The FIR was filed in SEM's c complaint under sections of criminal intimidation and threat. A senior police officer said, “They have been filing faulty surety bonds, and we can't accept them. We have to follow procedure. On Sunday evening, the SEM informed us he received threatening messages from CJP about the bail. He said he can't do the job under threat and at such risk. We have to delay the hearing. We have filed an FIR and are conducting an enquiry.” - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jignasa Sinha Jignasa Sinha is a Special Correspondent at Hindustan Times in New Delhi. With more than six years of reporting experience, she covers crime and policing in the national capital. Her beats also include Delhi prisons, the Delhi Fire Services and Delhi courts, while she regularly reports on gender, labour and social justice. Over the course of her career, Jignasa has reported on major criminal investigations, international crime syndicates, high-profile cyber fraud cases, law-and-order developments, protests, disasters and public institutions. Her reporting combines breaking news with in-depth, long form, human interest stories that examine the human impact of public policy, policing and the criminal justice system. In addition to reporting for the newspaper, she contributes to the Hindustan Times website and app, and plays an active role in coordinating on-ground coverage of major developments and breaking news across Delhi. Before joining Hindustan Times, Jignasa worked at The Indian Express newspaper in New Delhi, where she spent five years covering crime, Delhi airport, courts and health. news.headline: Maharashtra CM speaks to Tiger Shroff after assassination bid, dy CM Shinde says 'no gang will be spared'
news.story_lead: Maharashtra CM speaks to Tiger Shroff after assassination bid, dy CM Shinde says 'no gang will be spared' Deputy CM Eknath Shinde said the police had formed several teams to identify and arrest those responsible. Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday condemned the firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area and said he had spoken to the actor and also the Mumbai Police Commissioner to ensure the assailants were apprehended swiftly. Fadnavis sought details of the incident from police commissioner Deven Bharti and asked him to nab the assailants quickly, expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible, news agency PTI reported.
news.full_article_text: Maharashtra CM speaks to Tiger Shroff after assassination bid, dy CM Shinde says 'no gang will be spared' Deputy CM Eknath Shinde said the police had formed several teams to identify and arrest those responsible. Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday condemned the firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area and said he had spoken to the actor and also the Mumbai Police Commissioner to ensure the assailants were apprehended swiftly. Fadnavis sought details of the incident from police commissioner Deven Bharti and asked him to nab the assailants quickly, expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible, news agency PTI reported. "We are all with you. We will track down the accused soon. Do not worry," Fadnavis, who holds the Home portfolio, told the actor. Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also condemned the firing incident, calling it “deeply concerning”. He said he had spoken to both the Mumbai Police Commissioner and Shroff following the incident. Shinde said the police had formed several teams to identify and arrest those responsible, adding that the government would not tolerate attempts by gangs to spread fear in the city. Deep Dive “Tiger Shroff’s vehicle was targeted. This incident is deeply concerning and condemnable; I condemn it in the strongest possible terms. I have spoken with the Police Commissioner, and I have also spoken with Tiger Shroff. The Mumbai Police Commissioner has formed several teams to track down those who opened fire—they will be apprehended and given a response in their own language. Our current priority is to keep Mumbai and its citizens safe.” Emphasising that the safety of every citizen, regardless of whether they are a celebrity or an ordinary person, remained a top priority, he warned that those involved would face action and no gang would be spared. “Whether it is a celebrity or an ordinary citizen, ensuring their safety is the responsibility of the police and the government, and there will be no negligence in this regard. No gang will be spared; we will not let them get away with this." "We have seen large-scale gang wars like this before, back in the 1990s. Even then, the Mumbai Police effectively handled the situation—they dealt with the perpetrators in their own language, ensuring that law and order were maintained. So, any gang attempting to spread terror here should think twice. This is Mumbai; this is Maharashtra,” Shinde told reporters. ‘Criminals no longer fear law’: Supriya Sule NCP President Supriya Sule took a jibe at Maharashtra’s law and order situation, calling it ‘extremely alarming.” She questioned the situation of the state in which “criminals no longer fear the law” and urged the home minister to take appropriate measures to reassure the public. “An incident has come to light where actor Tiger Shroff was targeted in a shooting in Mumbai. Shootings are continuously surfacing across the state, and the situation is such that criminals no longer fear the law. Fortunately, while the actor was not injured in this incident, it is understood that some individuals sustained injuries," she wrote in a post on X. “In broad daylight, on busy streets, criminals are brandishing swords and firing shots. This picture of the law and order situation in Maharashtra is extremely alarming. As a result, citizens are living in fear and are anxious about their safety. I request the Honorable Home Minister to please immediately review the law and order situation in the state and take appropriate measures to reassure the public.” ‘Very sad’: Piyush Goyal Union minister Piyush Goyal called it a “very sad incident” and expressed confidence in police, saying necessary action will be taken to arrest the accused. “This is a very sad incident. I am confident that the police will take necessary action and arrest the accused,” he told news agency ANI. Congress leader Varsha Gaikwad also condemned the incident and raised concerns over Mumbai’s security and law-and-order situation. Citing previous incidents of firing outside actor Salman Khan’s residence and filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s residence, as well as the killing of veteran politician and Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) leader Baba Siddique, she questioned the safety of the city’s residents. "The firing was carried out by an unidentified person. However, this once again raises questions about how poor Mumbai's security and law-and-order situation has become. We have earlier seen firing outside Salman Khan's house. Unfortunately, Baba Siddique was shot dead, and firing also took place outside Rohit Shetty’s house. If Mumbai, the country's financial capital, whose police force was once compared to Scotland Yard, is in such a state, I want to ask: if politicians and actors are not safe in Mumbai, what will be the condition of the common man?” news agency PTI reported. AIMIM leader Waris Pathan also condemned the firing incident, raising concerns over Mumbai’s law-and-order situation and questioning how armed assailants could open fire in a crowded area such as Juhu. Pathan warned against a return to the era of underworld activity and threats to Bollywood personalities. He called for an immediate investigation and strict action against those involved, holding the government accountable for ensuring public safety. "In a place like Mumbai, on a Sunday, in the Juhu area, which is such a populated area where entire families visit Juhu Beach during the time of Navratri, some goons came to such a place and opened fire on Bollywood star Tiger Shroff, a young guy. ...What has happened to Mumbai? Do people want to take Mumbai back to the 90s era, when the underworld was active, film stars were threatened, and open firing took place? Shots were fired at Salman Khan, then at Rohit Shetty's home, and now this happened on a Sunday evening.” “What is the police doing? ...Whatever the extent of truth, this is a very serious and grave matter. The police should immediately conduct an investigation and take strict action against whoever is involved. We do not want Mumbai to go back to that era. Ensure safety, what is the government doing? When the government strays from its priorities, such incidents start happening. This is a total failure of law and order." According to preliminary information, three unidentified men on a motorcycle allegedly opened fire on the actor. Three people were reportedly injured, including the actor’s driver, who is said to have been struck by a bullet on his hand. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karishma Ayaldasani Karishma Ayaldasani is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, where she works with the digital team on fast-moving breaking stories from India and around the world. news.headline: CRPF chief lauds woman personnel for showing ‘resilience’ after being slapped during CJP protest
news.story_lead: CRPF chief lauds woman personnel for showing ‘resilience’ after being slapped during CJP protest The Delhi Police have filed an FIR against an unidentified protester for ‘slapping’ the official near Connaught Place on Friday during CJP's Tiranga march. The chief of the Central Reserved Police Force on Sunday commended a woman CRPF personnel for showing restraint on duty when she was allegedly heckled and assaulted by a woman protester on Friday during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s ‘Lehra Do Tiranaga’ march. CRPF director general (DG) GP Singh said the woman officer, who is a top judo practitioner and part of the CRPF’s judo team, displayed “extreme patience, perseverance and resilience” despite being assaulted.
news.full_article_text: CRPF chief lauds woman personnel for showing ‘resilience’ after being slapped during CJP protest The Delhi Police have filed an FIR against an unidentified protester for ‘slapping’ the official near Connaught Place on Friday during CJP's Tiranga march. The chief of the Central Reserved Police Force on Sunday commended a woman CRPF personnel for showing restraint on duty when she was allegedly heckled and assaulted by a woman protester on Friday during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s ‘Lehra Do Tiranaga’ march. CRPF director general (DG) GP Singh said the woman officer, who is a top judo practitioner and part of the CRPF’s judo team, displayed “extreme patience, perseverance and resilience” despite being assaulted. The Delhi Police have already filed an FIR against an unidentified protester who allegedly slapped and assaulted the official near Palika Bazaar, close to Rajiv Chowk Metro Station in Connaught Place on Friday evening during CJP's Tiranga march. The police on Saturday said that they registered at least three FIRs against protesters for allegedly violating prohibitory orders, taking out a flag march that affected law and order, and obstructing police personnel in the discharge of their duties. In a post on the incident, the CRPF chief, GP Singh said, “Reference assault on an on-duty CRPF Woman personnel by Anti-Social elements during a public order deployment in Delhi recently. Force leadership has complimented the CRPF personnel involved for showing extreme patience, perseverance and resilience despite being a top judo practitioner and part of CRPF Judo team. We remain committed to peace and order in the country. Lawful action is being taken by jurisdictional police in the matter.” The nine-second video, widely circulated on social media platforms on Saturday, shows the woman confronting the security personnel before slapping her. Police personnel can also be seen using whistles to disperse protesters. Delhi Police said they are identifying the woman for legal action in the matter. - Cockroach Janta Party

news.headline: Kolkata stampede: Accused sent to 10-day custody, officials suspended as blame game erupts after Chorbagan tragedy
news.story_lead: Kolkata stampede: Accused sent to 10-day custody, officials suspended as blame game erupts after Chorbagan tragedy Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari has said the government would set up an SIT headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta high court to probe into the incident. At least 19 people were killed and 25 were injured in a stampede at a prominent puja pandal in central Kolkata on Saturday evening. While police arrested seven persons and booked them under sections dealing with culpable homicide not amounting murder, West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the state government would set up a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta high court to probe into the incident.
news.full_article_text: Kolkata stampede: Accused sent to 10-day custody, officials suspended as blame game erupts after Chorbagan tragedy Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari has said the government would set up an SIT headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta high court to probe into the incident. At least 19 people were killed and 25 were injured in a stampede at a prominent puja pandal in central Kolkata on Saturday evening. While police arrested seven persons and booked them under sections dealing with culpable homicide not amounting murder, West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the state government would set up a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta high court to probe into the incident. Also read: Rain, a rush and a mic warning: The chain of events behind Kolkata’s Durga Puja stampede that killed 19 Deep Dive “The chief secretary will write to the Chief Justice of the Calcutta high court in this regard. It is up to the Chief Justice whether he allows a sitting judge to head the SIT. Else we will appoint a retired judge of the Calcutta high court to head the SIT,” Adhikari said. CM announces ex-gratia relief The chief minister announced government job and ex-gratia of ₹ 25 lakh for the next of kin of each of those who were killed in the accident. The injured would be given ₹ 5 lakh each and the state would bear their medical expenses. Also read: 'There was no way out': Families mourn loss of loved ones in Durga Puja stampede that killed 19 Union home minister Amit Shah, who had come to Kolkata on Saturday, cancelled all his puja-related programmes and visited the injured at the hospital. Of the 25 injured, two were admitted in the ICU with fractures. “I will try to visit the families who have lost their members on October 20 and 21,” Adhikari said. Later in day the chief minister held a high-level meeting with senior police officials and bureaucrats across the state to take stock of the security arrangements in big-ticket pujas. He also monitored crowd and traffic management in Kolkata and other cities in the state from the police control rooms. A committee headed by the state disaster management secretary and comprising officers from fire department and Special Task Force will visit the prominent pujas in Kolkata and make recommendations whether any rectifications need to be made. “If needed crowd will be restricted. There will be no separate queues for VIPs. We will do whatever it takes,” he said. Meanwhile, preliminary probe by the police revealed that an announcement by the puja organisers on Saturday evening that the Chorebagan pandal could collapse while urging people to vacate the pandal triggered the stampede. Also read: ‘Pandal will collapse, please leave’: Warning over mic set off Kolkata stampede, 19 dead The pandal which received an award from state government was registering heavy footfall over the past few days. On Saptami too thousands had thronged the pandal. “As rain hit pandal hoppers tried to take shelter inside the pandal. Those inside the pandal refused to go out. People also started to push in from the exit resulting in the chaos which ultimately the stampede started,” said a local resident. Row after Chorbagan stampede Allegations surfaced that there were not enough police at the scene, cops didn’t help the victims, there was no ambulance and locals had to book app cabs to help victims reach the hospital. "Who made these allegations? The victims, whom I spoke to at the hospital, gave a different version. They said the police helped them and booked cabs to send them to the hospital. The allegations are mainly against some home guards recruited two years back (during the previous government). Some of them don't even know Bengali and have a language barrier. I have asked for a list of the homeguards," Adhikari said. Also read: SIT headed by sitting judge to probe Kolkata pandal stampede; CM announces ₹ 25 lakh aid, government job The Mamata All India Trinamool Congress aggressively targeted the government with spokesperson and Kolkata MLA Kunal Ghosh focusing on the fact that old members of the Chorebagan puja committee stepped down after the BJP came to power in May. Ritesh Tiwari, state BJP spokesperson and MLA from Kolkata's Kashipur-Belgachhia constituency, defended his colleagues. "For decades, TMC MLAs and ministers such as Partha Chatterjee, Aroop Biswas and Firhad Hakim have been closely associated with community Durga Pujas. Before that, veteran Congress leader Somem Mitra was also associated with pujas. What is wrong if some BJP leaders are associated with some pujas? The chief minister has ordered a probe and the police have arrested several people," Tiwari said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Joydeep Thakur Joydeep Thakur is a Special Correspondent based in Kolkata. He focuses on science, environment, wildlife, agriculture and other related issues.

He also monitored crowd and traffic management in Kolkata and other cities in the state from the police control rooms. A committee headed by the state disaster management secretary and comprising officers from fire department and Special Task Force will visit the prominent pujas in Kolkata and make recommendations whether any rectifications need to be made. “If needed crowd will be restricted. There will be no separate queues for VIPs. We will do whatever it takes,” he said.
